questions.note: Order is right: the hallux longest, toe 2 clearly shorter, the 1–2 gap open, and toe 2 now has a PIP knuckle, a waist and a pulp. But the knuckle wrinkles are one stamp, toe 2's DIP crease is a single cut about 8 mm behind its nail so the tip reads finger-long, a seam rings toe 2 from below, the hallux lacks a base sulcus and a domed pulp, and the web is a shelf.

All the parts are there on both nails (edge thickness, pink bed, root crescent, rim), but they read as a press-on gel French manicure: a flat tile in an even gutter with exposed, proud sides, a crisp white root crescent, a wavy white stripe, a constant-width cream edge with squared slab corners; edges show past the pulps from below and a fleck glints under the hallux edge in clay.

In the scope the dorsum over the first MTP, the hallux and toe 2 is a smooth, oily surface: no EHL cord onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no veins, only a faint broad swelling at the frame's top; the one raised line there is a scar-like ridge across the MTP. The anchor feet show tendons and veins plainly.

The shader is a declared first pass; shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows. The relief is wrong in kind: one crumpled-cellophane crackle on dorsum, knuckles and web that glitters in highlights, straight corduroy ridges across ball and pads with no whorls, no follicle pits; with the oily dorsal sheen the toes read as a clean prosthetic.

defects.what: Both nails read as a gel French manicure: a crisp white crescent hugging the root, a wavy white stripe above the edge and a constant-width opaque cream free edge, alike on the hallux and toe 2.
defects.fix: A soft-edged pale lunula partly under the fold (clear on the hallux, faint on toe 2), a narrow pink-brown onychodermal band, and a translucent, faintly yellow free edge of slightly uneven width with a trace of grime under it.

defects.what: The hallux plate, like toe 2's, is a flat rounded-rectangle tile lying in an even gutter inside a uniform raised rim, its sides and root exposed and standing proud: a press-on, not a plate growing out from under its folds.
defects.fix: Curve the plate across its width (about 11 mm radius), tuck its sides under lateral folds that roll over them and its root under a proximal fold with a thin cuticle, so no gutter or plate edge shows except at the free edge.

defects.what: From below, a crisp straight seam with a glinting ridge rings toe 2 at the PIP and the outline steps in under it, so the toe's end reads as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4.
defects.fix: One or two short, slightly curved plantar flexion creases, soft-edged, with the proximal and middle pads bulging either side, the ridges continuing across them and no step in the outline.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin about 6 mm long that meets the hallux and toe 2 walls at corners: a shelf between the toes, seen also in both hallux views.
defects.fix: Give the web's free margin a soft U between the toes, deepest midway, rolling into each toe's side through a smooth fillet.

defects.what: From below, the hallux is a straight-sided capsule running out of the ball with no sulcus at its base and only a faint IP crease, so its pulp is not a separate oval dome.
defects.fix: A deep curved sulcus where the hallux pad meets the ball, a marked IP flexion crease, and a pulp bulging past it as an oval dome wider than the proximal pad, as in the anchor's soles.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four parallel, evenly spaced, equally crisp arcs; edge-on in the medial view they are comb-like ticks that ripple toe 2's knuckle outline.
defects.fix: Irregular knuckle wrinkles: one or two deeper lines at the joint and finer broken ones around them, of mixed length and depth, different on each toe, barely touching the outline.

defects.what: The dorsum over the first MTP and both toes is a smooth, oily surface: no EHL cord running onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no veins.
defects.fix: Low relief, 0.5–1.5 mm, of the EHL tendon over the first MTP onto the hallux's proximal phalanx and of the extensor slip to toe 2, with soft dorsal veins between, catching the rim light.

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 are bald: no dark hairs on either proximal phalanx, where a 40-year-old man's big toe carries a small tuft, as the anchor feet show.
defects.fix: 8–12 fine dark hairs, 5–8 mm long, lying flat distally on the hallux's proximal phalanx, and 2–4 shorter ones on toe 2's.

defects.what: A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum and shows edge-on in the medial view as two knife-cut ticks: it reads as a healed surgical scar, not a skin crease.
defects.fix: A few soft, short, irregular wrinkles over the MTP dorsum, or none; no raised ridge.

defects.what: Toe 2's distal segment reads finger-long: about 8–9 mm of bare skin lies between its DIP crease and its nail fold, where a second toe's nail starts 3–4 mm past the crease.
defects.fix: Put the crease over the DIP joint with the nail root just distal to it, so the nail covers most of a short, bulbous distal segment, as in the anchor close-up of toes.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip across most of the toe's width, a knife cut.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, broken creases over the joint, shallower toward the sides.

defects.what: The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle across the ball, the hallux pad and toe 2, running through the creases like corduroy.
defects.fix: Whorl or loop ridges centred on each pulp, a separate pattern on the ball, broken at each flexion crease and curving round the tips.

defects.what: The dorsal micro-relief is one crumpled-cellophane crackle of sharp facets, alike on knuckle, shaft and web, glittering in this highlight and visible on toe 2's dorsum at native size.
defects.fix: A soft furrow network of fine lines aligned with the creases and the toe's axis, with follicle pits, finer and fainter toward the tip, and no sharp facets in a highlight.

defects.what: In profile the hallux is about 21 mm deep at the IP and 18 at the nail root, against about 25 in Jeff's direction, so the 30 mm-wide toe reads flat and spatulate rather than a deep, round pad.
defects.fix: Deepen the hallux toward 25 mm at the IP, mostly in the plantar pad, so the pulp stays round in profile.

defects.what: At the zoom the hallux free edge ends at its corners in a squared, millimetre-thick opaque slab resting on the skin beside the fold.
defects.fix: Slightly rounded corners that thin and run into the lateral nail grooves, as on a nail trimmed straight across.

defects.what: From below, toe 2's free edge shows as a glassy sliver past its pulp, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its tip.
defects.fix: Trim so the free edges sit behind the pulps when seen from below, the pulps rounding past them.

defects.what: In clay a tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge suggests the plate's underside meets or pierces the hyponychium.
defects.fix: Keep the plate's underside clear of the hyponychium, with a thin shadowed gap under the free edge.

defects.what: In clay a hairline pinch runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall.
defects.fix: A soft concave fillet a few millimetres wide where the web turns into the toe's side.

ranked: [D1] Both nails read as a gel French manicure: a crisp white crescent at the root, a wavy white stripe and a constant-width cream edge. A man's toenail shows a soft, half-hidden lunula, a narrow pink-brown onychodermal band and a translucent, faintly yellow, uneven free edge.

[D2] The hallux plate, like toe 2's, is a press-on: a flat rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter, its sides and root exposed and proud. A real plate curves across its width and slips under the lateral folds and a cuticle-capped proximal fold.

[D3] From below a crisp seam with a glinting ridge rings toe 2 and the outline steps in under it, so the toe's end reads as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4; a plantar flexion crease is a soft fold with the pads bulging either side.
[D4] The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin, a shelf between the hallux and toe 2 in three views; a real web's margin is a soft U, deepest midway, rolling into each toe.

[D5] From below the hallux is a straight-sided capsule running out of the ball, with no sulcus at its base and a faint IP crease; a real big toe folds deeply into the ball and its pulp bulges past a marked crease as an oval dome.

[D6] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp, three or four parallel, evenly spaced, equally crisp arcs; in profile they become comb-like ticks rippling toe 2's knuckle. Real knuckle wrinkles are irregular, branching and of mixed depth.

[D7] The dorsum over the first MTP and the two toes is a smooth, oily mannequin surface: no EHL cord onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no veins, where the anchor feet show raised cords and soft veins even at rest.
[D8] The hallux and toe 2 are bald; a 40-year-old man's big toe carries a small tuft of dark hairs on its proximal phalanx, and toe 2 often a few, as several anchor feet show.
[D9] A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum, two knife-cut ticks in profile: a podiatrist reads a healed incision, not a crease.

[D10] Toe 2's distal segment reads finger-long: some 8–9 mm of bare skin between its DIP crease and the nail fold, where a second toe's nail starts just past the crease and covers most of a short, bulbous tip.
[D11] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even, bright-lipped groove across most of the toe, a knife cut rather than two or three short, soft, broken creases.

[D12] The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the ball, the hallux pad and toe 2, running through the creases like corduroy; pads carry whorls or loops centred on the pulp, broken at each crease.

[D13] The dorsal micro-relief is one crumpled-cellophane crackle of sharp facets, alike on knuckle, shaft and web and glittering in highlights; real toe skin shows a soft furrow network along the creases, with follicle pits, finer toward the tip.

Taken together the toes read young and pedicured, a foot model's or a silicone prosthetic's, not a boot-wearing 40-year-old soldier's: every surface clean and even, both nails glossy and symmetrical, no sign of wear anywhere in the scope.
[D14] In profile the hallux is about 21 mm deep at the IP against the 25 or so of Jeff's direction, so the broad toe reads flat and spatulate rather than a deep, round pad.
[D15] At the zoom the hallux free edge ends in squared, millimetre-thick opaque slab corners resting on the skin, where a trimmed nail's corners round off into the lateral grooves.
[D16] From below, toe 2's free edge shows as a glassy sliver past its pulp and the hallux's corners glint past its tip; trimmed toenails stay hidden behind the pulps from this view.
[D17] In clay a tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge suggests the plate's underside meets or pierces the hyponychium.
[D18] In clay a hairline pinch runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall instead of a soft concave fillet.
